en.t: Ever let an AI code suggestion take over without thinking?

chunks.tts_text: Ever let an AI code suggestion take over without thinking?

en.t: You see a suggestion pop up and hit Tab, trusting it feels easy.
But that shortcut can hide gaps in how you actually understand the code.

chunks.tts_text: You see a suggestion pop up and hit Tab, trusting it feels easy. But that shortcut can hide gaps in how you actually understand the code.

en.t: Metacognition means watching your own thinking, catching when you’re just going along.
When you accept a suggestion blindly, you skip the mental check that reveals whether it truly fits.
That missing check is the gap between feeling confident and actually knowing.
Seeing the gap makes you decide whether to adapt the suggestion or rewrite it your way.

chunks.tts_text: Metacognition means watching your own thinking, catching when you’re just going along. When you accept a suggestion blindly, you skip the mental check that reveals whether it truly fits. That missing check is the gap between feeling confident and actually knowing. en.t: In Koder, the CLI offers a one‑line fix as soon as you type a function name.
If you just press Enter, you get the code but you miss the chance to ask why it works.

chunks.tts_text: In Koder, the CLI offers a one‑line fix as soon as you type a function name. If you just press Enter, you get the code but you miss the chance to ask why it works.

en.t: Next time Koder suggests, pause and read the suggestion out loud.
Then ask yourself: does this solve the problem, and can I explain each part?
Write a quick comment summarizing the logic before you accept – that forces the mental check.
